proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the effective lag varies over time (or is closer to 0 weeks in some segments), a fixed 1-week delay can misalign peak timing and create brittle forecasts across split points.
proposals.rationale: Keep the current best template: SEIR with a 1-week reporting/admission lag via delayed_I. This matches the surveillance note about hospitalization lag while staying parsimonious and avoiding extra compartments/mixtures that were unstable in rolling splits.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Observation-map mismatch for a hospitalization-rate target: direct I may fit overall shape but systematically shift peak timing/scale relative to admissions, especially in high-peak weeks.
proposals.rationale: A controlled ablation of the delay: same SEIR structure but direct I observation to test whether explicit lag is necessary for this series. This reduces sensitivity to lag choice and may improve rolling stability if admissions track incidence closely at weekly resolution.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Weak identifiability in a short, single-season window: the added H dynamics can overfit peak height/width or produce unstable parameter tradeoffs with I, degrading rolling generalization.
proposals.rationale: Introduce an explicit hospitalization compartment while keeping the observation mapping simple (H only) and no delay. This directly targets hospitalization-rate semantics without composite observations, and changes only the structure relative to the baseline.
